entries.syllabusTitle: The origin and retention of Earth’s water

externalReferences.source: NASA — Bennu sample contains carbon and water
externalReferences.reason: Asteroid water-bearing materials can support the guide's explicitly limited asteroid-delivery hypothesis.
externalReferences.recommendedEdit: Keep as narrowly labelled evidence of possibility, not proof of the whole water inventory.

externalReferences.source: University of Oxford — Origin-of-water research, 16 April 2025
externalReferences.reason: Competing current research, broad origin-of-Earth context and habitable-zone material exceed A1.1.7's limited asteroid, gravity and condensation remit.
externalReferences.recommendedEdit: Remove research-news chronology and competing origin claims from core teaching; retain a short uncertainty caveat in optional notes only.

offendingMaterial.lessonExcerpt:
The required origin hypothesis in this syllabus is delivery by asteroids. Early Earth accreted material from the Solar System, and impacts by water-bearing asteroidal material could contribute water or water-forming ingredients. Water need not have arrived as liquid droplets; hydrated minerals can carry it chemically bound.
